## Account vs SPY
The account is ahead of SPY, not trailing. Whole account: $1,019.26 vs SPY-equivalent $1,008.21 — cumulative since inception +1.926% vs +0.821% (+1.105 points ahead over two days). Today alone the account gained +1.209% ($1,007.08 → $1,019.26) vs the SPY-equivalent's +0.561% ($1,002.59 → $1,008.21), which lines up with SPY's own close-to-close move of +0.56%. Most of today's edge over SPY is one sleeve, not broad skill (see "skill or luck" below).

Sleeves vs SPY (cumulative since 10-26, from `sleeve_equity.csv`): core +0.821% (0.000 vs SPY — it *is* SPY, a drawdown tool by design, adds nothing and isn't supposed to); dividend +0.821% (0.000 vs SPY — idle cash in SPY, adds nothing); earnings +0.857% (+0.037 vs SPY — essentially matching SPY, trivial, not a real edge); signals +2.449% (+1.628 vs SPY); momentum +6.522% (+5.701 vs SPY). Momentum's lead is the whole story for today's account-level outperformance (day return 153.25 → 159.78 = +4.26%, vs SPY's +0.56%), and it is not stock-picking: the current top-15 is concentrated in semis/storage (SNDK, MU, STX, WDC, INTC, MRVL, TER, HPE, LITE, DELL, AMD), and SMH (semiconductors) was +3.02% today — a sector day, not general SPY beta (betas to SPY logged on the 10-26 fills run 1.1x–5.3x but correlations are only 0.15–0.61, so SPY-beta doesn't even explain most of the move; the move tracks the sector, not the market). The rule is fully mechanical (quarterly 12-2 rebalance, no discretion today), so there's no judgment call to credit either way.

## Mistakes and misses
- **I missed CLS (+12.12% today).** It had three independent confirming sources — Q3 beat + raised 2026/2027 outlook, Bernstein Buy reiterated at $520, and a 12–17% premarket pop — more sourcing than CDNS got, but it was blocked by the 50-day filter (close 246.65 < 50-day 327.15). This is a rule filter, not a source gap or a timing failure: the rule did exactly what it's written to do. It still means a well-sourced catalyst in the middle of a long decline doesn't get bought under the current rule.
- **I missed AVGO (+4.00%).** Two independent sources (DA Davidson upgrade + the Anthropic S-1 financing disclosure) met the confirmation bar, but it failed the 50-day filter (329.17 < 355.48). Rule filter.
- **I missed SOFI (+13.42%).** The only no-buy reason logged was the 50-day filter (close 14.46 < 50-day 16.66). Rule filter. Shadow Test A did catch it as a gap-and-go day trade (gap +10.5%, rel vol 6.6x) but still lost money net, -0.228% after costs, entering at 10:37 ET — after the opening pop — and exiting at the 3:45 PM time stop; SPY's own return over that same window was +0.429%, so the shadow trade also trailed SPY. Timing and cost drag, not a missed opportunity in the real sleeves (SOFI was never eligible there).
- **UPS (+5.75%) and RCL (+5.46%) were correctly held back, not missed.** Each had only one confirming source, so the two-source confirmation rule wasn't met — a source gap, and the rule worked as intended (RCL's one source was itself mixed, with a Barclays PT cut alongside the beat).
- **No new unwritten-filter mistakes found today.** Every no-buy in `signal_log.csv` cites a written rule (50-day filter or the two-source confirmation rule) by name — unlike day 1's unwritten M&A exclusion.

## Overeager
**I acted on a signal type I haven't validated.** CDNS passed the expected-edge cost gate only as "pass (unknown expected gain)": `ev_gate_log.csv` says no backtest of the discretionary signals rules exists. It was well sourced (three independent confirmations, above the 50-day), but the signals sleeve as a whole is still an untested method, and today's CDNS gain doesn't change that. The other buy (DE) is a mechanical J4 earnings-run-up entry with a backtest behind it. No stock exits, no round-trips, no cluster of correlated buys like day 1's defense trio.

The one thing worth naming as overeager in a broader sense: two more shadow tests (VT, Test C) launched today, on top of the eight already running (A, B, Z, squeeze_bb30, X_orb15, X_orb30, X_vwap_reclaim, X_first_pullback) plus the pairs shadow, so about eleven parallel research threads now, with only a single day of data on the two newest. It's shadow-only, no paper money, and explicitly inside the owner's latitude, so it's not a rule violation — just a growing pile to keep honestly tracked.

## Too cautious
Nothing self-imposed found today. The CLS/AVGO misses above are the 50-day filter working exactly as written, not an extra, unwritten layer of caution I added on top of the rules.

## RULES.md compliance
No sizing or mechanics slips found today: CDNS was funded correctly from idle signals-sleeve SPY and sized at 10% of sleeve equity ($15.20 against a ~$152 sleeve); DE was sized at 5% of sleeve equity ($7.56) per the J4 rule, with its report date (2026-11-25 pre-market) and 20-trading-day entry window computed correctly. Both buys passed the EV cost gate and are logged in `ev_gate_log.csv`. Both carry beta60/corr60 per the v0.5.2 logging rule. Skip log: `skips.csv` has no rows today, which is correct — RULES.md only requires skip-log rows for capacity/no-quote/cost-check rejections, not for discretionary 50-day or confirmation no-buys (those live in `signal_log.csv`), same as day 1.

**I was wrong to call DE's logged beta (0.04, correlation 0.01) a likely data error.** I recomputed it from Yahoo adjusted closes (60 daily returns to 2026-10-23) and got the same 0.04 / 0.01. Over that window DE simply moved almost independently of SPY. The number is real, not a bug.

## Execution
Every fill today logs source, quote time and fee as required. Both close-run scripts (`sleeves.py close`, `shadow_check.py close`) ran clean, `shadow_errors.log` has no entries, and no exits or stops fired. 

## Shadow tests
- **Test A (gap-and-go):** 1 trade total (SOFI), net -0.228%, below SPY's same-window +0.429%. Pass bar needs 30+ trades, >+0.20%/trade, >half of weeks positive, t>1.5 — nowhere close, n too small for a t-stat.
- **Test B (RSI(2) swing):** 2 closed, 4 open/pending. Closed trades: 100% win rate, net/trade +1.249%, t 2.68 — "meeting the bar so far" per `shadow_summary.csv`, but the two closed trades (MPC, PSX) exited at today's open for small gains (+1.716%, +0.783%) right before both stocks fell -7.36% and -7.03% later in the day. That's exit-timing luck, not an edge, and n=2 is not a sample. Final verdict isn't due until week 8 — this is not passing yet.
- **Test Z (z-score dip):** 0 trades. Its own pre-registered backtest is already graded REJECT; nothing changed today.
- **squeeze_bb30:** 0 trades, no episode yet.
- **VT (vol-targeted core):** started today, value $399.40 vs a $400 hypothetical start (-0.15%, matching the entry cost). RULES.md is explicit that 0 of 8 weeks is an execution check only, not a performance read.
- **Test C (SPY calls 80/20):** 1 trade, 1 daily mark. Real book $997.61 vs mid book $998.80 (-0.239% net so far). First-day numbers look favorable against the pass bar (median |BS(VIX)−mid| 7.3% vs the ≤10% threshold; median quoted spread 0.6% vs the ≤2% round-trip threshold, well inside RULES.md's own pre-market "first look" estimate of 6–7.6%) — but this is one data point against an 8-week bar; it tells me nothing yet.

## What went well, skill or luck
CDNS is the one defensible pick today: three independent, named confirmations, the 50-day check applied correctly, and the lot is +4.28% after costs (fill $328.16, close $343.08), far more than its logged beta (1.55) times SPY's +0.30% open-to-close move would predict (about +0.47%) — an idiosyncratic, catalyst-driven move the process was built to catch. That's one data point, not proof of skill.
Momentum's +4.26% day was sector concentration (semis/storage riding SMH's +3.02% day), already covered above — not skill, since the rule is fully mechanical and made no decision today, and not simply "the market" either, since it's far beyond what SPY's own move explains. Core and dividend, both literally SPY, added exactly nothing by construction, as intended.

## Lessons (suggestions only)
1. The 50-day filter is costing well-sourced catalysts (CLS today, with three sources) when a name is still below its average after a long decline. Worth a shadow-only carve-out to track what a "3+ source, fails only the 50-day test" bucket would have done, rather than losing that data entirely. Rests on one example today.
